prompt: A tree has 20 nodes. How many edges does it have?
hint: Build a tree by adding nodes one at a time.
explanation: Every tree with n nodes has exactly n − 1 edges: 19. (Start with one node; each new node adds exactly one edge.)

verifier.code: const n=20; const E=h.range(2,n).map(i=> i+"-"+Math.floor(i/2)); const g=h.graph(E); if(Object.keys(h.bfsDist(g,"1")).length!==n) throw new Error("not connected"); return E.length;

prompt: Six people each shake hands exactly once with every other person. How many handshakes are there?
hint: Each handshake is a pair of people.
explanation: Choose 2 of the 6 people: C(6, 2) = 15.

verifier.code: return h.combinations(h.range(1,6),2).length;

prompt: A network has 8 computers, each connected by a cable to exactly 3 others. How many cables are there?
hint: Every cable has two ends.
explanation: The degrees add up to 8 · 3 = 24, and each cable is counted twice: 24 / 2 = 12 cables.

verifier.code: const n=8; const E=[]; for(let i=0;i<n;i++){ E.push(i+"-"+((i+1)%n)); if(i<n/2) E.push(i+"-"+(i+n/2)); } const deg={}; for(const e of E){ const [a,b]=e.split("-"); deg[a]=(deg[a]||0)+1; deg[b]=(deg[b]||0)+1; } if(!Object.values(deg).every(d=>d===3)) throw new Error("not 3-regular"); return E.length;

prompt: An unweighted graph has the edges listed. What is the smallest number of edges on a path from A to F?
code:
A — B
A — C
B — D
C — D
D — E
E — F
C — G
G — F
hint: Explore outward from A level by level.
explanation: Distance 1: B, C. Distance 2: D, G. Distance 3: E, F. Shortest path A–C–G–F has 3 edges.

verifier.code: const E=["A-B","A-C","B-D","C-D","D-E","E-F","C-G","G-F"]; return h.bfsDist(h.graph(E),"A").F;

prompt: Which node has the highest degree?
code:
A — B
A — C
A — D
B — C
C — D
C — E
D — E
hint: Count the edges at each node.
explanation: Degrees: A 3, B 2, C 4, D 3, E 2. C has the highest degree.

verifier.code: const E=["A-B","A-C","A-D","B-C","C-D","C-E","D-E"]; const deg={}; for(const e of E){ const [a,b]=e.split("-"); deg[a]=(deg[a]||0)+1; deg[b]=(deg[b]||0)+1; } const max=Math.max(...Object.values(deg)); const top=Object.keys(deg).filter(k=>deg[k]===max); if(top.length!==1) throw new Error("tie"); return top[0];

prompt: Roads with their lengths are listed (roads work in both directions). What is the length of the shortest route from A to D?
code:
A — B : 4
A — C : 1
C — B : 2
B — D : 1
C — D : 5
hint: The direct-looking route is not always the shortest.
explanation: A–C (1), C–B (2), B–D (1): total 4. Alternatives: A–B–D = 5, A–C–D = 6.

verifier.code: return h.dijkstra(["A-B:4","A-C:1","C-B:2","B-D:1","C-D:5"],"A").D;

prompt: A graph has nodes A, B, C, D, E and the edges A — B, B — C, C — D and B — E. Is it a tree?
hint: A tree is connected and has n − 1 edges.
explanation: It is connected (everything hangs off B) and has 4 = 5 − 1 edges, so it has no cycle: it is a tree.

verifier.code: const E=["A-B","B-C","C-D","B-E"]; const g=h.graph(E); const nodes=Object.keys(g); const connected=Object.keys(h.bfsDist(g,nodes[0])).length===nodes.length; return {index: connected && E.length===nodes.length-1 ? 0 : connected ? 1 : 2};

prompt: A robot walks along the lines of a 3 × 3 grid of squares from the top-left corner to the bottom-right corner, moving only right or down along grid lines. How many different routes are there?
hint: Count the ways to reach each grid point: add the counts from above and from the left.
explanation: Every route is 3 right-steps and 3 down-steps in some order: C(6, 3) = 20.

verifier.code: const n=3; const W=Array.from({length:n+1},()=>Array(n+1).fill(0)); for(let i=0;i<=n;i++) for(let j=0;j<=n;j++) W[i][j]= (i===0||j===0) ? 1 : W[i-1][j]+W[i][j-1]; return W[n][n];

prompt: Roads and their lengths are listed. What is the length of the shortest route from A to E?
hint: Use Dijkstra: repeatedly fix the closest town that is not yet fixed.
explanation: Final distances from A: B 7, C 9, F 11 (via C), D 20 (via C), E 20 (via C and F: 9 + 2 + 9). The shortest route A–C–F–E has length 20.

prompt: You must connect towns A–E with cables, using only the listed connections. What is the minimum total length of cable needed so that every town is connected?
code:
A — B : 4
A — C : 3
B — C : 1
B — D : 2
C — D : 4
D — E : 2
C — E : 5
hint: Repeatedly add the cheapest connection that does not create a cycle.
explanation: Kruskal: B–C (1), B–D (2), D–E (2), A–C (3). Total 8; every other cheap edge would close a cycle.

prompt: Can you trace every edge of this graph exactly once without lifting your pen? If so, where must you start?
code:
A — B
B — C
C — D
D — A
A — C
options: Yes, starting at A or C
Yes, starting at B or D
hint: Count the nodes with odd degree.
explanation: Degrees: A 3, B 2, C 3, D 2. Exactly two nodes have odd degree, so an Euler path exists, and it must start at one of them (A or C) and end at the other.

verifier.code: const E=["A-B","B-C","C-D","D-A","A-C"]; const deg={}; for(const e of E){ const [a,b]=e.split("-"); deg[a]=(deg[a]||0)+1; deg[b]=(deg[b]||0)+1; }const g=h.graph(E); const nodes=Object.keys(g); const connected=Object.keys(h.bfsDist(g,nodes[0])).length===nodes.length; const odd=Object.keys(deg).filter(k=>deg[k]%2===1).sort(); if(!connected) return {index:2}; if(odd.length===0) return {index:1}; if(odd.length!==2) return {index:2}; return {index: odd.join()==="A,C" ? 0 : 3};

prompt: The arrows show one-way streets. How many different routes lead from S to T?
code:
S → A
S → B
A → C
B → C
A → D
C → T
D → T
B → T
hint: Count the number of ways to reach each node from S.
explanation: Routes: S→A→C→T, S→A→D→T, S→B→C→T and S→B→T. That is 4.

verifier.code: return h.countPaths(["S>A","S>B","A>C","B>C","A>D","C>T","D>T","B>T"],"S","T");

prompt: Tasks have prerequisites: A before B, A before C, B before D, C before D, and D before E. Which order is valid?
hint: Check each order against every prerequisite.
explanation: A, C, B, D, E respects all five constraints. The others put D before C, B before A, or E before D.

verifier.code: const valid=h.topoOrders(["A","B","C","D","E"],["A>B","A>C","B>D","C>D","D>E"]).map(o=>o.join(", ")); return {indices: q.options.flatMap((o,i)=> valid.includes(o) ? [i] : [])};

prompt: A project has tasks with durations (in days): A 3, B 2, C 4, D 1. B and C can only start when A is finished; D can only start when both B and C are finished. Tasks without a dependency between them may run in parallel. What is the minimum number of days to finish the project?
hint: The project takes as long as the longest chain of dependent tasks.
explanation: A (3) then the longer of B (2) and C (4), then D (1): 3 + 4 + 1 = 8 days.

verifier.code: const dur={A:3,B:2,C:4,D:1}; const pre={A:[],B:["A"],C:["A"],D:["B","C"]}; const fin={}; const f=t=> fin[t] ??= dur[t] + Math.max(0, ...pre[t].map(f)); return Math.max(...Object.keys(dur).map(f));

prompt: Five towns lie on a ring road: each town is adjacent to exactly two others, forming a cycle A–B–C–D–E–A. Adjacent towns must get different colours on a map. What is the minimum number of colours needed?
hint: Try with 2 colours and go around the cycle.
explanation: Two colours would have to alternate around the cycle, which is impossible for an odd cycle of length 5. Three colours suffice (e.g. 1, 2, 1, 2, 3).

verifier.code: const E=[[0,1],[1,2],[2,3],[3,4],[4,0]]; for(let k=1;k<=5;k++){ if(h.tuples(h.range(1,k),5).some(c=> E.every(([a,b])=> c[a]!==c[b]))) return k; }

prompt: In the complete graph on 5 nodes (every pair of nodes connected), how many edges must you remove to be left with a spanning tree?
hint: How many edges does the complete graph have, and how many does a spanning tree on 5 nodes have?
explanation: The complete graph has C(5, 2) = 10 edges; a spanning tree on 5 nodes has 4. Remove 10 − 4 = 6.

verifier.code: return h.combinations(h.range(1,5),2).length - (5-1);

prompt: Breadth-first search starts at A. Neighbours are visited in alphabetical order. Which node is visited **fifth**?
code:
A — B
A — C
B — D
C — D
C — E
D — F
hint: BFS finishes all neighbours of a node before going deeper.
explanation: Queue: A → visit B, C → from B: D → from C: E (D already seen) → from D: F. Order A, B, C, D, E, F; the fifth is E.

verifier.code: const g=h.graph(["A-B","A-C","B-D","C-D","C-E","D-F"]); for(const k in g) g[k].sort(); const order=["A"], queue=["A"]; while(queue.length){ const u=queue.shift(); for(const v of g[u]) if(!order.includes(v)){ order.push(v); queue.push(v);} } return order[4];

prompt: The nodes of a graph form a grid of 3 rows and 4 columns; each node is connected to its horizontal and vertical neighbours. How many different shortest paths lead from the top-left node to the bottom-right node?
hint: A shortest path makes only right and down steps.
explanation: A shortest path has 2 down-steps and 3 right-steps in some order: C(5, 2) = 10.

verifier.code: const R=3,C=4; const E=[]; for(let r=0;r<R;r++) for(let c=0;c<C;c++){ if(c+1<C) E.push(r+"_"+c+"-"+r+"_"+(c+1)); if(r+1<R) E.push(r+"_"+c+"-"+(r+1)+"_"+c); } const g=h.graph(E); const d=h.bfsDist(g,"0_0"); const ways={"0_0":1}; const nodes=Object.keys(d).sort((a,b)=>d[a]-d[b]); for(const u of nodes) for(const v of g[u]) if(d[v]===d[u]+1) ways[v]=(ways[v]||0)+ways[u]; return ways[(R-1)+"_"+(C-1)];

prompt: Which list of degrees is **impossible** for a (simple) graph with 5 nodes?
hint: Add up the degrees.
explanation: The degrees always add up to twice the number of edges, so the sum must be even. 3+3+3+3+3 = 15 is odd: impossible. A 5-cycle gives all 2s, the complete graph all 4s, and a path gives 1, 2, 2, 2, 1.

verifier.code: const pairs=h.combinations(h.range(0,4),2); const seen=new Set(); for(let m=0;m<(1<<pairs.length);m++){ const d=[0,0,0,0,0]; pairs.forEach(([a,b],i)=>{ if((m>>i)&1){d[a]++;d[b]++;} }); seen.add(d.sort().join()); } const opts=[[3,3,3,3,3],[2,2,2,2,2],[4,4,4,4,4],[1,1,2,2,2]]; return {indices: opts.flatMap((o,i)=> seen.has([...o].sort().join()) ? [] : [i])};

prompt: A courier starts in A, must visit B, C and D (in any order) and return to A. The distances are listed. What is the length of the shortest round trip?
hint: There are only 3 · 2 · 1 = 6 orders (3 different round trips).
explanation: A–B–D–C–A = 2 + 4 + 3 + 9 = 18. The other round trips are A–B–C–D–A = 21 and A–C–B–D–A = 29. Minimum: 18.

verifier.code: const w={AB:2,AC:9,AD:10,BC:6,BD:4,CD:3}; const d=(x,y)=> w[x+y] ?? w[y+x]; return Math.min(...h.permutations(["B","C","D"]).map(p=> d("A",p[0])+d(p[0],p[1])+d(p[1],p[2])+d(p[2],"A")));

prompt: A graph has nodes A, B, C, D with edges A — B, B — C, C — D, D — A and the diagonal A — C. How many different spanning trees does it have?
hint: A spanning tree uses 3 of the 5 edges and must connect all four nodes.
explanation: There are C(5, 3) = 10 ways to choose 3 edges. Two choices form a triangle (A–B–C or A–C–D) and leave a node out. So 10 − 2 = 8 spanning trees.

verifier.code: const E=["A-B","B-C","C-D","D-A","A-C"]; return h.combinations(E,3).filter(s=> Object.keys(h.bfsDist(h.graph(s),"A")).length===4).length;

prompt: A hub H is connected to five towns that form a ring (each town is adjacent to its two neighbours on the ring and to H). Adjacent places need different colours. What is the minimum number of colours?
hint: The ring alone already needs 3 colours. What about H?
explanation: The 5-ring is an odd cycle and needs 3 colours. H is adjacent to all five towns, so it needs a fourth colour. 4 colours suffice.

prompt: Select **all** graphs that can be drawn by tracing every edge exactly once without lifting the pen.
code:
G1: A—B, B—C, C—D, D—A, A—C, B—D
G2: A—B, B—C, C—D, D—A, A—C
G3: A—B, B—C, C—A, C—D, D—E, E—C
G4: A—B, A—C, A—D
hint: A connected graph has such a path exactly when 0 or 2 nodes have odd degree.
explanation: G1 (a square with both diagonals): all four nodes have degree 3 — four odd nodes, impossible. G2 (a square with one diagonal): two odd nodes — possible. G3 (two triangles sharing a node): all degrees even — possible (even a closed tour). G4 (a star with 3 leaves): four odd nodes — impossible.

verifier.code: const Gs=[["A-B","B-C","C-D","D-A","A-C","B-D"],["A-B","B-C","C-D","D-A","A-C"],["A-B","B-C","C-A","C-D","D-E","E-C"],["A-B","A-C","A-D"]]; return Gs.map(E=>{ const deg={}; for(const e of E){ const [a,b]=e.split("-"); deg[a]=(deg[a]||0)+1; deg[b]=(deg[b]||0)+1; }const g=h.graph(E); const nodes=Object.keys(g); const connected=Object.keys(h.bfsDist(g,nodes[0])).length===nodes.length; const odd=Object.values(deg).filter(d=>d%2===1).length; return connected && (odd===0||odd===2); });

prompt: Roads connect the towns as listed. What is the minimum number of roads that must be closed so that you can no longer travel from A to F?
code:
A — B
A — C
B — D
C — D
B — C
D — F
C — E
E — F
hint: Look for a small set of roads that every route from A to F must use.
explanation: Every route leaves A via A–B or A–C, so closing those 2 roads disconnects A. One road is not enough: there are two routes, A–B–D–F and A–C–E–F, that share no road.

verifier.code: const E=["A-B","A-C","B-D","C-D","B-C","D-F","C-E","E-F"]; for(let k=0;k<=E.length;k++){ if(h.combinations(E,k).some(rem=>{ const g=h.graph(E.filter(e=>!rem.includes(e))); return !("F" in h.bfsDist(g,"A")); })) return k; }

prompt: Tasks and durations (days): A 3; B 2 (after A); C 4 (after A); D 2 (after B); E 3 (after C and D); F 1 (after E); G 5 (after B). Independent tasks run in parallel. What is the minimum project length in days?
hint: Compute the earliest finish time of every task.
explanation: Finish times: A 3, B 5, C 7, D 7, E 7 + 3 = 10, F 11, G 5 + 5 = 10. The project ends when the last task does: 11 days.

verifier.code: const dur={A:3,B:2,C:4,D:2,E:3,F:1,G:5}; const pre={A:[],B:["A"],C:["A"],D:["B"],E:["C","D"],F:["E"],G:["B"]}; const fin={}; const f=t=> fin[t] ??= dur[t] + Math.max(0, ...pre[t].map(f)); return Math.max(...Object.keys(dur).map(f));

prompt: Getting dressed has rules: underwear before trousers and before socks; socks and trousers before shoes; trousers and shirt before belt; shirt before tie; belt, tie and shoes before jacket. Many orders are allowed. Build the order by always putting on the **alphabetically first** item whose prerequisites are all done. What order do you get?
hint: Repeatedly pick the alphabetically first item whose prerequisites are all done.
explanation: Kahn's algorithm with alphabetical tie-breaking: shirt and underwear are free — shirt first. Then tie (needs shirt) vs underwear: tie. Then underwear, then socks and trousers become free: socks, trousers. Then belt and shoes: belt, shoes. Finally jacket.

verifier.code: const N=["belt","jacket","shirt","shoes","socks","tie","trousers","underwear"]; const E=[["socks","shoes"],["trousers","shoes"],["underwear","trousers"],["trousers","belt"],["belt","jacket"],["shirt","belt"],["shirt","tie"],["tie","jacket"],["shoes","jacket"],["underwear","socks"]]; const done=[]; while(done.length<N.length){ const free=N.filter(x=> !done.includes(x) && E.every(([a,b])=> b!==x || done.includes(a))).sort(); done.push(free[0]); } return {order: done.map(x=> N.indexOf(x))};
